Stock Buy: High-Octane
Earnings At A Discount
Sep 01, 2026 at 12:00 PM ET | PBF Energy Inc. (PBF) Stock
Summary
Seeking Alpha
Investing Group Leader
This #1 Quant-rated Energy stock is positioned to
beneﬁt from tight global fuel supplies and an
undersupplied California market.
Strong Q2 results were supported by robust fuel
margins, the Martinez reﬁnery restart, lower costs,
and rapid balance-sheet improvement.
Despite its strong momentum, this stock trades at a
steep discount to the sector and offers a 1.51%
forward dividend yield supported by strong dividend
safety metrics.
The company’s earnings outlook strengthened
sharply, with analysts issuing 10 upward FY1 estimate
revisions and no cuts over the past 90 days.
The Alpha Picks portfolio continues to outperform the
broader market, returning +344.63% versus
+103.18% for the S&P 500 since its inception in July
2022, and YTD 21.53% versus 12.47%, respectively.

Business Overview
zhudifeng/iStock via Getty Images
PBF Energy Inc. (PBF) is the #1 Quant-rated Energy stock
and one of the largest independent petroleum reﬁners and
suppliers of unbranded transportation fuels, heating oil,
and other petroleum products in the United States. PBF
operates through two primary segments:
Reﬁning: The company’s core earnings engine,
which converts crude oil into gasoline, diesel, jet fuel,
heating oil, asphalt, and other products.
Logistics: Conducted principally through wholly
owned PBF Logistics LP (PBFX), which owns or
leases terminals, storage facilities, pipelines, rail- and
truck-unloading assets, and related infrastructure
used to support the movement of crude and reﬁned
products.
PBF Energy operates a highly complex reﬁnery network,
enabling it to process a broad slate of crude oils—from
light, sweet grades to heavier, sour grades—and optimize
product yields and feedstock economics. The company
also has meaningful exposure to renewable-fuel and
environmental-credit economics, particularly in California.

Our Buy Thesis
PBF operates six reﬁneries with an aggregate crude-
throughput capacity of approximately 1.0 million barrels
per day. Its network includes facilities in Delaware City,
Delaware; Paulsboro, New Jersey; Toledo, Ohio;
Chalmette, Louisiana; Torrance, California; and Martinez,
California. The footprint provides exposure to major U.S.
reﬁned-product markets on the East Coast, Gulf Coast,
Midwest, and West Coast and provides access to a range
of domestic and imported crude grades through
waterborne, pipeline, rail, and truck infrastructure.
A key differentiator for PBF is its high concentration of
assets on the U.S. West Coast, particularly the Torrance
and Martinez reﬁneries in California. The Martinez reﬁnery,
which experienced a devastating ﬁre in late 2024, has
since resumed operations as of May 2026, restoring the
company's full operating capacity. These West Coast
facilities now operate in a structurally underserved market
following the closure of two competing California reﬁneries,
strengthening PBF’s position.
PBF is more focused on reﬁning than many of its larger
peers, giving it more direct exposure to changes in reﬁning
margins and crack spreads. Reﬁning margins represent
the proﬁt earned by converting crude oil into products such
as gasoline, diesel, and jet fuel. Crack spreads are a
widely followed measure of reﬁning economics, reﬂecting
the difference between crude-oil costs and the market
value of the reﬁned products.

This reﬁning-focused model can make PBF’s earnings and
share price more sensitive to fuel-market swings, but it
also creates meaningful upside when crack spreads
widen. The company has beneﬁted from an unusually
favorable reﬁning environment as disruptions in the Middle
East and reduced ﬂows through the Strait of Hormuz have
tightened global supplies of gasoline, diesel, and other
products. PBF management has said that disruptions in
the Strait of Hormuz constrained crude supplies to Asian
reﬁners, which normally serve markets including the U.S.
West Coast. The resulting reduction in reﬁned-product
availability has further tightened global markets, and
management expects reﬁning fundamentals to remain
supported by tight balances and low product inventories
worldwide.
“Product inventories will be slow to rebuild and the
restocking that ultimately must occur should provide a
favorable backdrop for reﬁning margins over the
quarters to come,” said PBF CEO Matt Lucey.
The company is also well positioned to beneﬁt from wider
crude-quality differentials. PBF’s complex reﬁneries can
process substantial volumes of medium- and heavy-sour
crude, and management has highlighted that greater
availability of these barrels—including from OPEC+ supply
increases and Venezuelan exports—can lower feedstock
costs relative to lighter crude benchmarks.
Beyond the current geopolitical backdrop, PBF’s longer-
term opportunity rests on a structurally constrained U.S.
reﬁning industry. Industry capacity rationalization and
limited new reﬁnery construction have tightened the supply
outlook, while demand for transportation fuels remains
resilient. This dynamic is especially pronounced in
California, where reﬁnery closures have increased the
state’s dependence on fuel imports and enhanced the
strategic value of PBF’s Torrance and Martinez reﬁneries.

PBF Stock Growth and Proﬁtability
PBF Stock Earnings Revisions, Momentum, and
Valuation
Seeking Alpha’s Quant Factor Grades assess companies
relative to others in their sector. PBF earns particularly
strong marks for growth, momentum, and revisions. The
stock also trades at a hefty discount relative to other
energy stocks, accompanied by improving proﬁtability.
PBF Stock Factor Grades
Seeking Alpha, as of 9/1/2026
PBF entered the second half with all reﬁneries operating
well, including the fully restored Martinez facility. The
company reported a strong second quarter, with adjusted
earnings of $6.22 per share and adjusted EBITDA of $1.24
billion, exceeding consensus estimates. PBF showcases
exceptional growth, supported by 13.5% Y/Y revenue
growth, which is 23% above the energy median,
accompanied by 268% FWD operating cash ﬂow growth
vs. 9% for the sector.
Strong demand and tight fuel supplies supported robust
reﬁning margins, while the company improved its balance
sheet by reducing net debt by more than $1.4 billion during
the quarter. Operational initiatives are also gaining traction:
lower energy use, better turnaround execution, and
procurement savings are expected to reduce annual costs
by roughly $60 million. PBF’s ROE exceeds the sector
median by 95% while the company holds $7.54 in cash per
share.

PBF Energy’s earnings revisions grade has staged a
remarkable turnaround, improving from a ‘C-’ six months
ago to an ‘B+’ today. The upgrade reﬂects strengthening
fundamentals and a far more constructive outlook for the
business. Analyst sentiment has turned unanimously
positive; over the past 90 days, all 10 revisions to FY1
earnings estimates have moved higher, with no downward
revisions.
PBF Revisions Grade
Seeking Alpha, as of 9/1/2026
Improving fundamentals and upward analyst revisions
have fueled strong price momentum in PBF shares. Price
momentum is a highly predictive indicator that can signal
growing investor conﬁdence in the company’s outlook.
PBF Momentum Grade
Seeking Alpha, as of 9/1/2026
Although PBF’s price momentum has lifted the shares
toward 52-week highs, the stock still trades at an excellent
valuation. A range of metrics remain heavily discounted
relative to the sector, including a trailing 12-month P/E and
forward price-to-cash-ﬂow ratio that are 62% and 56%
below their respective sector medians.
PBF Valuation Grade

Seeking Alpha, as of 9/1/2026
PBF also offers a solid forward dividend yield of 1.51%, an
important consideration for income-oriented investors. The
dividend appears well covered by the company’s cash
generation, as its cash-to-dividend payout ratio is 63%
below the sector median, indicating a conservative payout
burden and capacity to sustain the dividend over time.
PBF Dividend Safety Grade

Potential Risks
Concluding Summary
Seeking Alpha, as of 9/1/2026
PBF faces the risk that the reﬁning environment could
reverse. Its earnings are highly sensitive to fuel margins,
which may decline if global reﬁning capacity returns,
product inventories rebuild, demand softens, or crude price
differentials become less favorable. The company also
remains exposed to volatile oil prices, freight costs, and
renewable fuel credit expenses, which can pressure
proﬁtability even when fuel demand is healthy.
Operational risks are equally important. Reﬁnery outages,
accidents, weather disruptions, maintenance delays, or
supply-chain constraints can reduce throughput and
increase costs. PBF also operates in heavily regulated
markets, particularly California, where evolving
environmental rules, permitting requirements, and low-
carbon fuel policies could require additional spending or
limit ﬂexibility. While debt has fallen sharply, a weaker
margin cycle or higher capital needs could slow further
balance-sheet progress.

PBF Energy is one of the largest independent U.S.
reﬁners, with a broad network of reﬁneries and logistics
assets serving key fuel markets across the country. The
company is well-positioned to beneﬁt from tight global fuel
supplies, constrained reﬁning capacity, and especially
favorable conditions in California following the restart of its
Martinez reﬁnery. PBF’s improving operational
performance, strengthening balance sheet, and cost-
reduction initiatives support a more constructive earnings
outlook. The stock boasts excellent Quant factor grades
for growth, proﬁtability, momentum, and earnings revisions,
while still trading at an attractive valuation and offering a
1.51% forward dividend yield.

Alpha Picks performance from July 1, 2022 through
July 30, 2024 is calculated using a notional buy-
and-sell methodology: picks are purchased at the
opening price on the pick date and removed at the
closing price on the exit date. Beginning July 31,
2024, performance is calculated using volume-
weighted average price for both purchases and
sales. S&P 500 performance is calculated starting
July 1st, 2022, and is based upon buying an equal
amount of SPY on the pick date using the opening
